items.stem: In an experiment, what is the independent variable?

options.text: The one factor the investigator deliberately changes
options.rationale: Correct: the independent variable is the one you change on purpose.

options.text: The factor you measure as the outcome
A factor you keep the same for fairness

options.rationale: That is an error, not a variable.

items.explanation: Correct: the independent variable is the one you change on purpose.

items.stem: A student changes the temperature AND the amount of water at the same time and gets a result. Why is this a problem? (Select ONE)

options.text: You cannot tell which change caused the result, so the test is not fair
options.rationale: Correct: changing two variables makes the cause unclear.

options.text: Using water is never allowed in experiments
options.rationale: Water is fine; the issue is changing two variables.

options.text: Results are only valid if nothing is changed at all
options.rationale: You must change the independent variable to test it.

options.text: Temperature cannot be measured accurately ever
options.rationale: Temperature can be measured; that is not the issue.

items.explanation: Correct: changing two variables makes the cause unclear.

items.stem: Select TWO ways to make the results of an experiment more reliable. (Select TWO)

options.text: Repeat each measurement and compare the readings
Keep all control variables the same across trials
options.rationale: Correct: controlling variables keeps the test fair and reliable.

options.text: Change the method differently in every single trial
options.rationale: Changing the method each time reduces reliability.

options.text: Record only the result you were hoping to see
options.rationale: Recording only preferred results is biased and unreliable.
